High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench

Court No. - 11
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 814 of 2024

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Prin. Secy. Deptt. Of Home Lko

. And Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Abhishek Dwivedi
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Rajesh Singh Chauhan,J.

1. Heard Sri Abhishek Dwivedi, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Ajeet Singh Gaharwar,
learned Additional Government Advocate for the State.

2. In view of the order proposed, the notice to opposite party No.2 is hereby dispensed with.
3.

By means of this anticipatory bail application, the applicant has prayed for grant of anticipatory bail in Case Crime No.17 of 2024, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 & 409 I.P.C. and Section 66-D of Information Technology (Amendment) Act,2008, Police Station-Alambagh, District-Lucknow.

4. However, after arguing the matter at some length, learned counsel for the applicant has confined his prayer to the effect that the present applicant may be permitted to appear before the learned court concerned within a period of two weeks and may file his regular bail application and direction Prince Kumar Singh (In Fir Army No. ... vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Deptt. Of ... on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179666497/
1 may be issued to the learned trial court concerned to dispose of such regular bail application with expedition without giving any unnecessary adjournment to the prosecution.

5. Considering the aforesaid innocuous request of learned counsel for the applicant, on that the learned Additional Government Advocate has no objection, the liberty is given to the present applicant to appear/surrender before the learned trial court concerned within 15 days from today and file his regular bail application and if the present applicant appears/ surrenders before the learned trial court concerned within the aforesaid stipulated time and files his regular bail application, such regular bail application may be decided by the learned trial court concerned with expedition, strictly in accordance with law by affording an opportunity of hearing to the parties concerned and without giving any unnecessary adjournment to the prosecution.
6. In view of the aforesaid observations and directions, the instant anticipatory bail application is disposed of finally.

[Rajesh Singh Chauhan,J.] Order Date :- 16.4.2024 Suresh/
